text:
Maria Chen: quick check-in — noticed a handful of tenants showing persistent 50-150ms window_skew in the continuous batcher telemetry. wondering if the tenant-stitching logic is the culprit or something upstream. anyone seen this pattern?
Ajay Patel: saw a spike last night, yes. looks like requests with stitch_key set are getting delayed until a matching prefix arrives. suspected cause: our current stitch buffer holds onto partial windows for 200ms by default.
Samir Rao: 200ms is large if traffic is bursty. the original rationale was to improve packing for small tenants, but it does amplify skew when tenant arrival rates are variable.
Maria Chen: right. tradeoff: longer buffer -> better packing and throughput, but higher tail latency for early requests. short buffer -> worse token-efficiency.
Leo Martinez: ops note: the skew correlates with GC pauses on older instances (heap spikes), but also with multi-tenant mixing — when a heavy tenant interleaves with many small ones. hard to disentangle.
Ajay Patel: two quick options: 1) per-tenant adaptive buffer: shrink for tenants with high arrival variance; 2) make stitch buffer queue soft-limit and proactively flush after X requests or time. 1) needs per-tenant metrics and state.
Samir Rao: per-tenant state increases memory pressure. we already saw headroom issues when we tracked per-tenant kv caches. memory blowup is a real risk under spike.
Maria Chen: thoughts on a middle ground: maintain a small fixed buffer (e.g. 30ms) globally but allow a lightweight tenant-score that lets us extend buffer for "pack-friendly" tenants. score can be an EWMA of inter-arrival times (coarse bucketed).
Ajay Patel: EWMA score idea sounds promising. low-cardinality state. bucket by tenant-tier (free/pay) + recent traffic band. avoids full per-tenant heavy state.
Samir Rao: agree, but need eviction semantics for the stitch-map entries. propose TTL+LRU cap (e.g. max 5k entries per worker) and a fast-path that bypasses stitch if map is full. that avoids OOM but hurts packing in rare cases.
Maria Chen: also want to instrument a new metric: "stitch_bypass_rate" and "stitch_eviction_cause" (ttl|cap|policy). helps correlate with skew spikes.
Leo Martinez: +1. also add a histogram of window_wait_time labeled by tenant_tier and worker_id. this will show if skew is concentrated per-worker.
Ajay Patel: quick experiment plan: roll a config with stitch_buffer_ms=30, stitch_ttl=500ms, stitch_map_cap=5000, enable EWMA scoring. run on 10% fleet for 6h, compare pack efficiency and p99 latency.
Samir Rao: can we add a fallback: if EWMA indicates high variance, tag tenant requests with header "stitch-expected:false" so downstream runtime skips stitch and goes straight to fast-path. avoids waiting.
Maria Chen: good call. pragmatic fallback reduces risk. action items: Ajay to prototype scoring + config flags, Samir to add eviction/bypass fast-path and metrics, Leo to add histograms in observability. I'll coordinate rollout and postmortem checklist.
infra-bot: deploy triggered by Ajay P. Config set: experiment.stitch_buffer_ms=30 for canary group. :rocket:
Ajay Patel: starting prototype; will ping here with perf snapshots.
Maria Chen: thanks all — keep replies short in this thread for traceability. we'll reconvene after the 6h canary. :thumbsup:
